attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. The quoted tweets in the post are other people's, but the train-wreck characterisation is his.

semantics.note: A firm description of the summit's reception on 10 Feb 2025. 'From everything I can tell from afar' says where his information came from; it is not a probability hedge. 'Almost everyone' and the conflicting reasons are kept.

contract.note: Reading 'almost everyone' as near-universal dissatisfaction is the ordinary reading of his firm words, though it may be hyperbole. Treating 'train wreck' as evaluative and scoring the checkable dissatisfaction claim is fair. The result depends on what counts as 'almost everyone'.

evidence.note: Criticism of the leaked draft dated 8 Feb, before the target date. It shows some experts objected, but not how widespread displeasure was on 10 Feb.
Same-day report of different views on regulation and of labour concerns. It fits the 'conflicting priorities' part but does not show displeasure with the summit itself, or how many were displeased.
Pichai's prepared speech, a company publication, speaks positively of the summit's conversations. This is weak counterevidence: one participant's statement cannot show how most stakeholders felt.

reviews.rationale: There is no representative or systematic measure of stakeholder satisfaction on 10 Feb 2025. The packet shows criticism of the draft beforehand, conflicting policy priorities, and one favourable industry participant. That is not enough to establish near-universal dissatisfaction or to rule it out.
